title: Test what an AI answer means, not only how it's worded
short: Test what an AI answer means with Driftline checks
description: Driftline's drift test scores how close two answers are in wording. Checks (must_include, must_not_include and same_fields) let you say what has to stay true, so a changed meaning fails the test.

blocks.p: Driftline's drift test runs each of your prompts on the current model and on its replacement and scores how similar the two answers are. The score reads wording, not meaning: "is eligible" and "is not eligible" share almost every word. Checks let you say what has to stay true, and a prompt that fails one is marked broken.
Add them to any prompt in `.driftline/prompts.yml`:

blocks.code:
prompts:
  - id: refund-reply
    prompt: ...
    must_include: [refund, "5 business days"]
    must_not_include: ["not eligible"]

  - id: invoice-json
    expect: json
    prompt: ...
    same_fields: [status, total, customer.id]

ul: **`must_include`**: each phrase must appear in the new answer.
**`must_not_include`**: none of these phrases may appear.
**`same_fields`**: for prompts with `expect: json`, these fields must keep the current model's value. Use dots for nested fields.

blocks.p: Phrases ignore case and spacing. Lists can also be written with one item per line.

table: Similarity 0.90 or higher, and every check passed
Similarity 0.60 to 0.90, or an answer gains or loses a "not", or a check the current model fails too
Similarity below 0.60, JSON that no longer parses, or a check the new answer fails

blocks.p: If the current model fails the same check, that isn't drift, so the prompt is marked changed instead of broken.

blocks.h2: Why it matters for the fix pull request

blocks.p: With `fix-pr: true`, the pull request carries a verdict from your prompts. It says "safe to merge" only when your prompts have checks. Without checks it says the wording stayed close, which is a weaker claim.

Start with the 5 to 20 prompts your app really sends, and add a check to the ones where a wrong answer costs something: a refund policy, a label, a total. The drift test makes two API calls per prompt on your own key, so ten prompts on a weekly schedule is 20 calls a week.
Checks are part of [Driftline Pro](/#drift). The scan and the fix pull request are free. The [README](https://github.com/AI-Driftline/driftline#checks) has the full syntax.
